title: How can moving a point divide a number?
description: A hundred and twenty three, twenty four, six hundred and seventy eight and twelve are divided by ten, a hundred or a thousand by moving the decimal point to the left. Keeko doubts that twelve divided by a thousand is zero point one two.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the zeroes in the divisor and move the point that many places to the left, adding zeroes in front when the digits run out. Watch for students who move the point fewer places than there are zeroes.

source: Use the rule of moving the decimal point to find 123 ÷ 10, 24 ÷ 100, 678 ÷ 1000 and 12 ÷ 1000
video_script.why: The child has met division by ten, a hundred and a thousand as thousandths and now sees a quick rule for it.
video_script.substitution: the book's four divisions, with the book's own three steps of the rule
video_script.anchor: Four divisions from the book: a number is divided by ten, a hundred or a thousand by moving the decimal point to the left
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip gives twelve divided by a thousand as zero point one two. The point has moved only two places, but a thousand has three zeroes, so the point must jump a third place over an added zero.
video_script.payoff_line: Each number is now divided by moving the point.

final_answer.spoken: twelve point three, zero point two four, zero point six seven eight and zero point zero one two

maths_rules: the rule: write the number with a point at its end, count the zeroes in the divisor, move the point left by that many places, add zeroes in front if needed
123 ÷ 10: 10 has 1 zero, the point moves 1 place left, 123. becomes 12.3
24 ÷ 100: 100 has 2 zeroes, the point moves 2 places left, 24. becomes 0.24
678 ÷ 1000: 1000 has 3 zeroes, the point moves 3 places left, 678. becomes 0.678
12 ÷ 1000: 1000 has 3 zeroes but 12 has 2 digits, a zero is added in front, 12. becomes 0.012
the slip: 0.12 = 12 ÷ 100, which is ten times 12 ÷ 1000
video_script.design: One idea: the zeroes of the divisor say how many places the point jumps left. Assumes place value and the hidden point of a whole number. Wrong idea: two places for a division by a thousand. The four divisions stay all video; each step moves a point on a number; the numbers after the jump appear only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks twelve divided by a thousand is zero point one two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But in that answer the point has moved only two places. A thousand has three zeroes.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The point must jump three places, so a zero is added in front. The answer is zero point zero one two.
